answer.rationale: Onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%) are both down this quarter, and two inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) directly claim durable lifts from onboarding simplification. These are the most causally proximate levers to the observed metric declines, so I verify them first since they're older records being relied on for a real decision. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but matching aggressive entry pricing risks a margin/value race-to-bottom that could hurt 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' even if it defends short-term acquisition — so I'm flagging that risk rather than acting on it this week. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives don't address the acute onboarding/activation drop. With only one experiment slot, I favor a small guarded test of onboarding simplification to confirm the inherited finding still holds in the current environment before considering a broader rollout, rather than treating memory_31/memory_86 as settled fact.
